model_annotation: This plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several language model variants, comparing their convergence behavior. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks spaced every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis shows the loss value, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks every 0.1 unit. Six lines are plotted, each corresponding to a different model configuration: Vanilla (purple, solid line), StrmLLM (n=64, blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H, green, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H/T, red, solid line), and SepLLM (n=128, dark blue, solid line). All lines start near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline initially, followed by a gradual decrease as iterations progress. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest loss, stabilizing around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The StrmLLM (n=64) model shows the highest loss throughout, stabilizing near 2.6. The other SepLLM variants lie between these two, with SepLLM (n=64, H/T) and SepLLM (n=64, H) converging to losses around 2.52–2.53, while SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=128) converge slightly higher, around 2.53–2.54. All lines show some noise or fluctuation, particularly at the beginning, but overall trends are smooth and monotonically decreasing.
